sec: Fulminant hepatitis and the SAAG quadrant map · p1005

items.q: The feature of ascites in fulminant hepatitis is:
opts: Ascites with a chronic PHTN picture
items.exp: Fulminant hepatitis: ascites without chronic picture (PHTN). (Book p1005)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed as causes of fulminant hepatitis . The odd one out is:
items.exp: Listed causes: paracetamol / alcohol / mushroom / rat killer poisoning; aflatoxin is not on the p1005 list. (Book p1005)

items.q: SAAG (serum ascites albumin gradient) = S. albumin minus:
items.exp: SAAG: serum ascites albumin gradient = S. albumin − ascitic fluid albumin (AFA). (Book p1005)

items.q: A SAAG ≥ 1.1 defines high-SAAG ascites, which account for what proportion of ascites ()?
items.exp: ≥ 1.1 : high SAAG ascites (90%) d/t PHTN. (Book p1005)

items.q: A SAAG < 1.1 defines low-SAAG ascites (10%), due to:
items.exp: < 1.1 : low SAAG ascites (10%) d/t peritoneal membrane permeability. (Book p1005)

items.q: Match the four SAAG × protein quadrants — 1) High SAAG, high protein 2) High SAAG, low protein 3) Low SAAG, high protein 4) Low SAAG, low protein … A) ↓ protein synthesis, ↑ loss : nephrotic syndrome B) Through hepatic vein — BCS (Budd–Chiari) C) Any peritoneal cause, m/c : peritoneal CA D) ↑ Sinusoidal pressure
items.exp: High SAAG + high protein (↓AFA, ↑protein): through hepatic vein — BCS; high SAAG + low protein (↓AFA, ↓protein): ↑ sinusoidal pressure; low SAAG + high protein (↑AFA, ↑protein): any peritoneal cause, m/c peritoneal CA; low SAAG + low protein (↓protein synthesis, ↑loss): nephrotic syndrome. (Book p1005)

items.q: In the high-SAAG, high-protein quadrant, what directional changes in serum-ascites albumin difference and fluid protein concentration occur?
items.exp: High SAAG, high protein: ↓ AFA, ↑ protein (through hepatic vein — BCS). (Book p1005)

items.q: ‘In low-SAAG, high-protein ascites the ascitic fluid albumin (AFA) is reduced.’
opts: False — that quadrant is ↑ AFA with ↑ protein (peritoneal causes, m/c peritoneal CA)
True — AFA is reduced in every low-SAAG pattern
False — the AFA is normal in peritoneal disease
True, but only in nephrotic syndrome
items.exp: Low SAAG, high protein: ↑ AFA, ↑ protein (cause: any peritoneal cause, m/c peritoneal CA). (Book p1005)

items.q: A paracentesis gives SAAG 2.0 g/dL and ascitic protein 4.0 g/dL, with the AFA well below the serum albumin. Which quadrant and aetiology fit?
opts: High SAAG, high protein — Budd–Chiari through the hepatic vein
High SAAG, low protein — sinusoidal pressure
Low SAAG, high protein — peritoneal CA
Low SAAG, low protein — nephrotic syndrome
items.exp: SAAG ≥ 1.1 + high ascitic protein (↓AFA, ↑protein) = the BCS quadrant, not the usual cirrhotic low-protein pattern. (Book p1005)
